title: Constant strict towers and normalized derived direct image

source.place: Proof Step 5, proper/direct-image generator and final normalization paragraph

proof.text: Work on the diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] for the index category $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$. The tower category is abelian with exact evaluations by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Choose a K-injective representative $M\to J_M$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The functor $\Delta$ is right adjoint to the exact evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_1$: a map from a tower to a constant tower is uniquely determined by its component at $1$, and the other components are forced by the transition maps. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $\Delta J_M$ K-injective. For the constant coefficient rings, [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identifies module pullback with exact geometric inverse image; its right adjoint is the module direct image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] also makes $f_*J_M$ K-injective. On this representative the termwise direct image is literally $f_*\Delta J_M=\Delta(f_*J_M)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] identifies it with the derived termwise direct image. This gives the natural isomorphism $\chi_{f,M}:\Delta(Rf_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_f^{\mathcal T}(\Delta M)$. Evaluating the displayed literal equality at every $n$ gives the identity of $Rf_*M$, proving clause (2).

proof.text: On the same diagonal K-injective representative, the ordinary inverse limit of the constant tower is $J_M$, so the derived inverse limit $\mathcal L_X(\Delta M)$ is canonically $M$, and similarly $\mathcal L_Y(\Delta Rf_*M)$ is $Rf_*M$, by the K-injective computation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The comparison $a_{f,\Delta M}$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] is induced by the underived equality $f_*\lim=\lim f_*^{\mathcal T}$. For a constant tower this equality is the literal identity on $f_*J_M$, and the source and target identifications are the two canonical diagonal limit identifications just described. Therefore $\mathcal L_Y(\chi_{f,M})^{-1}\circ a_{f,\Delta M}$ is the identity, proving clause (3).

proof.text: Let $Q_{\bullet}=(\underline{P_n}_Y)_n$. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $K_M\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], independently of $J_M$ in Step 1. Under [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], tensor products and total tensor complexes are computed componentwise: evaluate the sheaf tensor universal property at each diagram index. For any acyclic tower complex $B$, every $B_n$ is acyclic, and $(B\otimes\Delta K_M)_n=B_n\otimes K_M$ is acyclic; exact evaluations detect acyclicity by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus $\Delta K_M$ is K-flat and $(K_M\otimes_{\underline A_X}\underline{P_n}_X)_n$ represents $\mathcal R_X(M)$ with its quotient augmentation. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], the exact termwise pullback carries $Q_{\bullet}$ to $(\underline{P_n}_X)_n$, compatibly with every quotient map; exactness means that its derived pullback has this same value. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the diagram ringed-topos morphism, $E=\Delta M$, and $P=Q_{\bullet}$. Using its canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and precomposing with $\chi_{f,M}\otimes1$ identifies its source with $\mathcal R_Y(Rf_*M)$ and its target with $R_f^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_X(M)$. This is the specified map $h_{f,M}$.

proof.text: Naturality in the coefficient argument and the tensor-unit normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] applied to the strict quotient map $\Delta\underline A_Y\to Q_{\bullet}$ give, before taking any inverse limit, the equality of tower morphisms $h_{f,M}\circ i_{Rf_*M}=R_f^{\mathcal T}(i_M)\circ\chi_{f,M}$. Indeed the projection for the tensor unit is the identity on the diagonal direct image, while the two vertical arrows are exactly the quotient augmentations; the diagonal direct-image identification is the literal map used to define $\chi_{f,M}$ in Step 1. Thus the displayed equality is the required clause (4), with all maps normalized by the same counit-tensor construction.
